CLINICAL FEATURES OF FURUNCULOSIS (BOILS)
Clinical Features
- Can be found on all body sites where hairs are present. It starts with a small,
yellow creamy pustule that rapidly evolves into a red nodule, often with a
central yellow plug
- As the lesion expands, it becomes painful and tense
- Associated with local oedema, lymphangitis, regional lymphadenopathy
and fever
- Eventually, the central part of the nodule becomes soft and drains
spontaneously
- Healing occurs after about 1 - 2 weeks with scar formation
